client_brief:
Apex Rally Club: Apex face system

Project overview
The Apex Rally Club is a volunteer amateur motorsport club in Vermont. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Apex face system, six designs in two reductions plus crest colourways and Reference sheet masters and metal ground.

What we will provide
apex_reference_sheets/ (6 frames, 4000 x 3000); apex_crest_jacket.jpg (3024 x 4032); apex_backing_card_2025.pdf; apex_designs.csv (6 rows); apex_mint_requirements.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Apex face system, six designs in two reductions plus crest colourways: Six club faces recovered from photographed printed reference as placeable scalable geometry with transparent grounds, a real viewBox present and no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along. 
- Reference sheet masters and metal ground: The six reference sheets straightened and brought to one ink density target so the set is comparable, with a per sheet parameter log, plus one licensed camera scale struck metal frame graded to sit with the faces. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$1,200-$3,200 fixed; target delivery 7 to 15 business days; one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

price_band_and_audience: A two tier collectible line: twelve dollar impulse pins across a tent table and ninety five dollar numbered coins bought by members aged roughly twenty to forty five who already own the previous years. The band is load bearing and it splits the artwork in two. A struck coin at ninety five dollars has to carry fine raised line work and tight registration a member inspects in the hand, while a twelve dollar hard enamel pin has wells a mint must be able to fill, so detail below a certain weight has to be deliberately taken out rather than left in and hoped for. Treat the whole set at pin level and the coin reads as a giveaway and the numbered edition collapses; treat the pin at coin level and the mint cannot strike it, the enamel bleeds its wells and the tent table sells a defect. The register overall is club rather than corporate: confident and worn in rather than slick, never novelty and never distressed for effect, because the ninety five dollar buyer is buying continuity with 1987. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Volunteer run amateur rally club producing hard enamel pins and struck challenge coins for its members and event tent table
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1987 in Vermont; a volunteer run club of two hundred and forty members holding six events a year
brand_identity.about: The Apex Rally Club is a volunteer amateur motorsport club in Vermont. Six events a year, and a merch table that pays for the timing gear. The club crest goes back to 1987 and each event badge, the hillclimb, the night stage, the ice trial, the gravel loop and the finale, was drawn over the years by members. This autumn is our first proper collectible run with a mint.
brand_identity.audience: Club members aged roughly twenty to forty five who already own the previous years and buy on continuity with the club's history, plus impulse buyers at the event tent
brand_identity.price_positioning: A two tier line: twelve dollar impulse pins across the tent table and ninety five dollar numbered coins a member inspects in the hand. The register is club rather than corporate: confident and worn in, never novelty and never distressed for effect.
brand_identity.typography: A worn slab or industrial serif for crest and badge lettering, carried as outlined vector, paired with a plain sans for the mint spec sheet, capsule insert and backing cards. The feel is club regalia with a straight face, history rather than novelty.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, understated and proud of the years behind us; we talk about continuity, not hype. Example line the brand would write: "Same crest we ran in 1987, struck to hold up to the light."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: None of the art exists in a form a mint will accept. What we have is six reference sheets, the crest and five event badges, printed at different times on different paper and photographed on a workbench under whatever light was in the garage. A member also sent a photo of the crest as it is embroidered on the club jackets. The mint requirements file gives diameters, the hard enamel colour ceiling, plating options and the rule that the coin's raised metal version must be line only.
brand_identity.values: Continuity with 1987: the ninety five dollar coin is bought on history, so the faces have to read as one club collection rather than six separate files, worn in but never sloppy.

assets_supplied.name: apex_reference_sheets/ (6 frames, 4000 x 3000)

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the six recovered faces are a set. Stroke weight in a traced outline is a function of how heavy the ink reads in the raster the trace received, not of how the badge was drawn, so six sheets printed at different times and photographed under different light trace into six outlines of visibly different line weight, each of which looks completely right while it is being looked at alone. The trace reports nothing: no weight, no threshold, no simplification, and an identical response for a heavy face and a spindly one. The mismatch exists only in the comparison, at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the mismatch is a property of the relationship between six finished traces and cannot exist until all six exist. Doing it right first time presumes knowing, per sheet, how much ink density to add or remove before a trace that has no controls, which nothing reports. Nothing states it either: the client describes the photographs, not what a trace does with them. It is not a propagation re run, because the fix reaches back to per sheet preparation for specific faces only.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which faces sit heavy and which thin against the set, go back to the ink density preparation for just those sheets, re trace, redo the hygiene, and lay the six out together again at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mint receives six faces that are supposed to be one collection and cuts six dies at three different line weights, which on a numbered ninety five dollar coin sold on continuity with 1987 is exactly the defect the buyer holds it to the light to look for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each backing card is actually carrying its own design. Two things are knowable only by running the merge: whether the printer's flat card converted into a layout that can carry a different picture per record at all, which depends on how the original file was built rather than on what the printed card shows, and whether the per record proofs are in the order they claim. The proofs render, they carry a label naming their row, and that label can be wrong while every file reports success, so a run named by position ships the ice trial's face on the gravel loop's card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because both facts exist only after a conversion and a merge that have already happened, and no parameter controls either. Nothing states it, since the client says the shape is right and the design changes. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different delivery route chosen for identity, plus a verification pass that reads each proof's own content against its row.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Establish identity by what is printed on each proof, re derive the per SKU files through a route whose ordering is trustworthy, reconcile the two rows pointing at one artwork file, and re check all six.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six hundred pins reach a tent table on backing cards carrying the wrong design's face and the wrong edition size, which is a reprint of the whole run and a refund line at the event the pack was made for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the colourway decision rests on. The committee has to judge the crest colourways on struck metal, so the natural construction is the face carried over the metal ground with a sheen and an edge treatment that read as struck rather than printed. Those constructions do not survive intact: blending against the ground and layered edge treatment are normalised away or truncated, silently, at full success, so the face can arrive as a flat opaque shape on a photograph of metal. The returned markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition shows the first canvas only.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports. Nothing states it: the client asks to see the colourways on the metal, which is art direction rather than a warning. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different upstream asset or a treatment rebuilt from the constructions that do survive.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the colourway page around a construction that survives the import, re author, re run the readiness check, export again, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A committee votes on a flagship coin colourway from a page where the crest is a flat shape on a picture of metal, picks the option that looks best flat, and the mint strikes the one that reads worst in the hand.

decision_gates: Whether the embroidered crest is admissible evidence at all, and which crest version is the club's when the two disagree about a year band.
How much correction to spend making six garage lit sheets comparable before any is traced, given that the trace has no controls at all.

Whether the printer's card can carry a per record picture at all, and what to deliver instead if it cannot.
How to reconcile two rows pointing at one artwork file before anything is bound, and how to normalise the inconsistent price and edition cells without editing the client's meaning.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the sheets into a frontier image model and it returns six handsome motorsport badges. IDENTITY: these are this club's actual crest from 1987 and five badges drawn by named members, worn on jackets and already owned by two hundred and forty people, so a regenerated badge is a different club's badge and the ninety five dollar coin is sold precisely on continuity with what already exists.
